I am a Research Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics at Dartmouth College. I develop
data-driven and operator-theoretic methods for understanding and predicting complex nonlinear systems,
with applications ranging from weather and climate to plasma physics and neuroscience.

My current work combines Koopman operator theory with ideas from quantum mechanics, including quantum
computing, to extract patterns from data, build reduced models and assimilate observations. Examples
include the El Niño–Southern Oscillation, the Madden–Julian Oscillation and organized convection. I
work with collaborators in mathematics, physics and the climate sciences.

I trained as a physicist at the University of Warsaw, and worked at NYU and NYU Abu Dhabi, Rutgers,
the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee and the University of Helsinki before joining Dartmouth in 2022.
